question: Should `@openclaw/krillswitch-react/server` and `FeatureFlagProvider.initialValues` be accepted as stable public React SDK APIs with the documented SSR fallback and cache-precedence semantics?
rationale: This is a new exported SDK capability rather than a repair to an established contract, and the decision determines the long-term supported API shape and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Approve the stable SSR API
options.body: Treat the server evaluator and hydration bootstrap as supported public SDK surface, then complete normal code review and documentation checks.

options.title: Keep the concept internal for now
options.body: Avoid exporting the server entry point until maintainers choose an experimental or narrower SSR integration boundary.

options.title: Request a narrower contract
options.body: Retain the SSR goal but revise the API or precedence semantics before committing to public support.

recommendation.title: Approve the stable SSR API
recommendation.body: Treat the server evaluator and hydration bootstrap as supported public SDK surface, then complete normal code review and documentation checks.
